q: What is a characteristic of a Type 1 hypervisor?

o.A: It is referred to as a hosted hypervisor.
o.B: It is completely independent of the operating system.
o.C: Problems in the base operating system can affect the entire system.
o.D: It is installed on an operating system and supports other operating systems above it.

q: What is a characteristic of a Type 2 hypervisor?

o.A: It is completely independent of the operating system.
o.B: It is installed on an operating system and supports other operating systems.
o.C: It eliminates the need for an underlying operating system.
o.D: Its main task is to manage hardware resources between different operating systems.

e: A characteristic of a Type 2 hypervisor is that it runs on top of a host operating system. Unlike Type 1 hypervisors, which run directly on the physical hardware, Type 2 hypervisors are hosted within a standard operating system environment. This means that the Type 2 hypervisor relies on the underlying host operating system to manage hardware resources and provides virtualization capabilities as an application or software layer.

q: SIMULATION: Fix the LACP EtherChannel/trunk between Sw10 and Sw20 and force Sw10 to be STP root for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. Make changes on Sw10 only.
tasks: Sw20 is actively attempting to negotiate an 802.1 trunking EtherChannel with Sw10 using LACP, but the channel is not functional. Resolve the issues on Sw10.
Modify the spanning tree configuration to ensure that Sw10 is always the root for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
e:
Task 1 (fix LACP EtherChannel to Sw20 and make it a trunk):
conf t
interface range e0/0, e0/1, e0/2
 shutdown
 no channel-group
 switchport
 no shutdown
 channel-group 10 mode active
!
interface port-channel 10
 switchport
 switchport mode trunk
 no shutdown
end

Task 2 (force Sw10 to always be root for VLAN 10 and 20):
conf t
spanning-tree vlan 10 priority 0
spanning-tree vlan 20 priority 0
end

q: SIMULATION: Extend the Finance VRF between R11 and R22 using Tunnel 10 and configure static routing so traffic between VLAN 111 and VLAN 222 uses Tunnel 10 exclusively. Configure R11 only.
tasks: Extend the Finance VRF between R11 and R22 using Tunnel 10.
Complete the Finance VRF configuration on R11 and configure static routing so that traffic between VLAN 111 and VLAN 222 uses Tunnel 10 exclusively.
e:
Task 1:
R11(config)# ip vrf Finance
R11(config-vrf)# rd 100:1
R11(config-vrf)# route-target export 100:1
R11(config-vrf)# route-target import 100:1
R11(config-vrf)# exit
R11(config)# interface Tunnel 10
R11(config-if)# vrf forwarding Finance
R11(config-if)# ip address 10.10.100.1 255.255.255.252
R11(config-if)# tunnel source 208.165.200.1
R11(config-if)# tunnel destination 208.165.201.4

Task 2:
R11(config)# interface e0/1
R11(config-if)# vrf forwarding Finance
R11(config-if)# ip address 10.10.111.1 255.255.255.0
R11(config)# ip route vrf Finance 10.10.222.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.100.2

Validation on Sw11: ping 10.10.222.1

q: Which two characteristics apply to Type 1 hypervisors? (Choose two.)

o.A: They are widely available to license for free.
o.B: They provide a platform for running bare metal operating systems.
o.C: They can be used to create and manage virtual storage.
o.D: They are a software layer that runs on top of a virtual server.
o.E: They provide a platform for running guest operating systems.

e: Type 1 hypervisors can create and manage virtualized storage resources, which are used by the virtual machines (VMs) running on the platform. Type 1 hypervisors run directly on the hardware (bare metal) and provide an abstraction layer for guest operating systems, allowing multiple OS instances to run concurrently on the same physical hardware.

q: In a virtual environment, what is an OVA file?

o.A: A zip file connecting a virtual machine configuration file and a virtual disk.
o.B: A file containing a virtual machine disk drive.
o.C: A configuration file containing settings for a virtual machine such as a guest OS.
o.D: A file containing information about snapshots of a virtual machine.

e: An OVA (Open Virtual Appliance) file is essentially a single file that contains a complete virtual machine. It is a tarball that includes: the virtual machine configuration file (OVF), one or more virtual disk images (VMDK), and optional resource files or metadata.

q: In a virtual environment, what is a VMDK file?

o.A: A zip file connecting a virtual machine configuration file and a virtual disk.
o.B: A file containing a virtual machine disk drive.
o.C: A configuration file containing settings for a virtual machine such as a guest OS.
o.D: A file containing information about snapshots of a virtual machine.

e: A VMDK (Virtual Machine Disk) file is used by VMware to store the contents of a virtual machine's hard disk. It includes the operating system, applications, and data, functioning like a physical disk drive for the VM.

q: What is VXLAN?

o.A: Layer 3 overlay that is switched with a Layer 2 underlay scheme encapsulated with MAC-in-TCP.
o.B: Layer 2 overlay that is routed over Layer 3 and encapsulated with MAC-in-TCP
o.C: Layer 2 overlay that is routed over Layer 3 and encapsulated with MAC-in-UDP
o.D: Layer 3 overlay that is switched with a Layer 2 underlay scheme encapsulated with MAC-in-UDP

e: VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) is a Layer 2 overlay technology designed to extend Layer 2 networks over a Layer 3 underlay. It uses MAC-in-UDP encapsulation, allowing virtual machines in different physical locations to appear on the same Layer 2 segment.

q: What is the VXLAN network identifier used to identify?
e: VXLAN uses the VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) as a 24-bit field to uniquely identify a Layer 2 segment (broadcast domain) over the Layer 3 underlay. Each VLAN in the traditional network maps to a VNI in VXLAN, enabling scalable segmentation.

q: Which entity serves as a VXLAN tunnel endpoint?
e: A VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP) is the device that encapsulates and decapsulates VXLAN traffic, serving as the endpoint of the VXLAN tunnel.
